content.text: LOGOS writes an action as an **event**. ∃e says there is an event e. Run(e) says that e is a running, and Agent(e, John) says that John does it.
Past(e) puts the event in the past. ∧ means and: every part describes the same event e.

examples.note: There was a running, John did it, and it is in the past.
The Theme is who or what the action is directed at. Here it is Mary.
HAB marks a habit: Mary sleeps, as a rule. LOGOS reads many present tense verbs this way.

question.hint: Start with ∃e. Say what kind of event e is, who did it, and that it is past.
question.explanation: Sleep(e) names the event, Agent(e, Mary) says Mary did it, and Past(e) puts it in the past.
